fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responding units can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly to indicate it is the only vehicle access point to the property.
• Post a site map at the driveway entrance showing the locations of all structures on the property.
• Create a vehicle turnaround area near the end of the driveway so emergency vehicles can reposition without reversing the full length of the drive.
• Keep the full width of the driveway clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and overgrown vegetation so emergency vehicles can travel its full length without obstruction.
• Trim tree branches and shrubs along both sides of the driveway to maintain clearance for tall emergency vehicles.
• Assign a visible number or letter marker to each detached structure so responders can quickly identify and communicate which building they are operating at.
• Clear a walking path connecting all structures so responders can move between buildings on foot without having to return to the driveway.
• Cut back dense vegetation near each detached structure to keep a clear zone around doorways and access points.
• Identify and mark a rear access point to the property, even if only suitable for foot traffic, and communicate its location to your local fire station.
• Mark the location of the water feature with a visible sign so responding units can identify it at night or

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang over or touch the roof and walls of any structure in the cluster.
• Thin trees within the scattered clusters nearest to the structures to create open gaps between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against the foundation or walls of any structure.
• Separate shrubs from one another where they grow in continuous patches near the structures.
• Clear low-hanging branches from trees along the driveway to keep the travel lane open for vehicles.
• Cut back shrubs and tall grass along both sides of the driveway so vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Thin or remove vegetation growing in and along the drainage channel where it runs close to any structure.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from within the irrigated landscape beds near the structures.
• Keep the area immediately around each structure in the cluster free of loose woody debris, cut branches, and piled yard waste.
• Trim shrubs near the structures so they do not connect visually or physically with nearby trees.
• Clear vegetation from around any outbuildings or secondary structures in the cluster to create open ground between them and surrounding plants.
• Keep the driveway entrance clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs so emergency vehicles can enter without delay.
